explainBack.question: Why does the government argue that copying newspaper articles to train an AI can be fair use, when copying an article to republish it clearly would not be?
explainBack.answer: Because fair use is judged per use, not per act of copying. When articles are used in training, software adjusts numerical settings to extract statistical patterns of language; the purpose is building a tool that generates responses, not delivering those articles to readers. Republishing serves the same purpose as the original and substitutes for it, so the same copying gets a different legal question — just as recording a programme to watch later differs from selling the tape. And the filing itself concedes an output that reconstructs and distributes a work can raise yet another question.

explainBack.assessment: The article fully supports this answer: mechanism, purpose distinction, use-by-use framing and the output caveat are all present in the reader's ordinary language.

unseenTransfer.scenario: A software vendor pitches your team a writing assistant, saying: 'Our model was trained entirely on licensed data, so anything it writes is copyright-safe for you to publish under your brand.'
unseenTransfer.question: Using this article's mental model, is the vendor's conclusion sound?
unseenTransfer.answer: No. The article's stage separation shows training legality and output legality are different questions. Even a lawfully trained model can produce an output that closely reconstructs an existing work, and publishing that output is a distinct use judged on its own — purpose, amount taken, market effect. The right move mirrors P011: before publishing any close-match output, ask what the basis is for using that specific passage, because a claim about training does not answer a question about your proposed use.
unseenTransfer.expectedEvidence: The obtain/train/output pipeline (P005), the output-reconstruction caveat (P009), and the training-claim-doesn't-answer-use-question move (P011).
unseenTransfer.assessment: The article's mechanism resolves this genuinely new scenario correctly and specifically, so transfer is demonstrated.
